title: CRITICAL: cost budget reads only the first page, so budgets never trip
description:
FOUND BY A RUNAWAY RUN THAT COST \$49.31 AGAINST A \$25 BUDGET. Budget enforcement is effectively disabled for any run exceeding 50 model calls.

Evidence from run_f15efdfb79a84bda9914e92a39395f3d:
  recorded cost_usd  \$2.98
  actual gateway     \$49.31 across 887 calls, 45.7M input tokens
  configured budget  RUN_MAX_COST_USD = 25
The run passed its budget nearly 2x and kept going for ~4.4 hours until stopped by hand.

ROOT CAUSE, reproduced against the live API. gateway.ts pagination:
    const totalPages = payload.result_info?.total_pages ?? 1;
    if (entries.length < LOG_PAGE_SIZE || page >= totalPages) break;
The AI Gateway logs API does NOT return total_pages. Its result_info is:
    {"count": 50, "page": 1, "per_page": 50, "total_count": 845}
So total_pages is undefined, defaults to 1, and `page >= 1` breaks on the FIRST iteration every time. Exactly one page — 50 entries — is ever counted. \$2.98 of \$49.31 is 6%, which is 50/845.

FIX: derive the page count from total_count and per_page, or simply keep paging while entries.length === LOG_PAGE_SIZE. Do not trust a field the API does not send. Add a test that pins the real result_info shape (no total_pages) and asserts more than one page is fetched — the existing tests must have used a fixture that invented total_pages, which is why this passed.

ALSO FIX THE CLASS, not just the line: MAX_LOG_PAGES=20 x 50 caps counting at 1000 calls, and this run made 887. A long run will silently under-count again once it passes 1000. Either page until exhausted, or treat hitting the cap as a telemetry FAILURE (which jk7 already makes a refusal) rather than as a complete total — an under-count that looks like a total is exactly what made this cost money.

WORTH CHECKING WHILE THERE: the same undercount feeds runs.cost_usd, so every cost figure this factory has ever reported is low by the same mechanism.

acceptance_criteria: A run with more than 50 model calls reports its true gateway spend; a cost budget trips at the configured amount, proven against a fixture with the REAL result_info shape; hitting the page cap is treated as a telemetry failure rather than a total; a regression test pins the no-total_pages response.
closed_reason: Completed: the gateway cost query pages until exhausted instead of trusting a total_pages field the API never sends — the bug that let a run bill $49.80 against a $25 budget while reporting $2.98 — and hitting the page cap is now a telemetry failure rather than a total.
